name: ENSIGN GROUP, INC
moat_justification: A real, replicated operating system (local-leader turnarounds of distressed facilities) that has held ROIC at 17–25% for six years, plus owned real estate through the captive REIT — but prices are set by government payors, labor is regulated and inflating, there are no switching costs, and the June 2026 short-seller allegations attack the durability of the cost advantage itself. Moderate moat, not wide.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base

OVERRIDE_APPLIED:capex — filing gap in the last 3 FY filled by a judgment override (filing: Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025, Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows, investing activities line 'Purchase of property and equipment': $(193,557) thousand for FY2025, $(158,240) thousand for FY2024 and $(106,180) thousand for FY2023 (statement in thousands)); an override never replaces a filed value — see overrides_applied and override_impact
BASE_DIVERGENCE: latest FY OE/share 5.48 vs 3-yr median 2.66 — one of them is distorted; find out which and why
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 5.1x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
TIER_BAND: bear-case tier D (7.4%) vs bull-case tier C (11.7%) — the verdict spans tiers; size any position to the bear end
one_liner: Proven skilled-nursing turnaround operator, moat 6/10 — but at $173.05 the price already pays for the super-bull path: weighted IRR 9.6% and weighted IV@15% $90.80, so it clears 15% only below ~$91; the unresolved June 2026 understaffing / administrator-license allegations and the securities class action sit on top of a full price.
exit_alert_suppressed_reason: tier exists only because of a judgment override
moat_for: Turnaround playbook replicated for 26 years: buys distressed 1–2-star facilities and lifts them — CMS data published Feb 2026 shows same-store survey results 24% better than state peers and a 19% advantage in 4–5-star buildings
ROIC proxy of 17–25% in every year FY2020–FY2025 (fundamentals.json), earned through a full reimbursement and labor cycle
Decentralized local-leader model with cluster density: 373 facilities across 17 states at FY2025 year-end, with shared Service Center overhead a single-facility operator cannot match
Standard Bearer captive REIT: 158 owned real-estate properties at FY2025 year-end give cost control plus a rent-based earnings stream on top of operations
Demographic tailwind: an aging population drives skilled-nursing and post-acute demand independent of the economic cycle
moat_against: No pricing power: Medicare/Medicaid set the rates — the payor is the price-maker
Labor is the product and the cost: staffing is regulated, scarce and inflating; gross margin slid from 23.1% (FY2021) to 20.1% (FY2025)

June 2026 Hunterbrook and Muddy Waters reports allege margins partly rest on understaffing and rented administrator licenses at an estimated ~20% of facilities — if even partly true the cost advantage is neither durable nor lawful; a securities class action followed (Perusek v. The Ensign Group, C.D. Cal., lead-plaintiff deadline Dec 7, 2026)
No switching costs: patients, hospital referrers and staff can all leave; the turnaround model is replicable by any disciplined operator
Growth is substantially bought: 102 operations added since 2024 — acquisition pricing and integration are permanent execution risks
Repeat False Claims Act history: a $48M settlement in 2013 and the 2023 relator settlement behind the $60.8M litigation expense in FY2023 earnings
